own_inspection: For a symmetric code range[-7,7], maximum=7, so scale=M/7. Per-channel here means reduce dimension1 and retain row dimension0; scalar scale shape[] or row scale shape[2,1] broadcast correctly to[2,4].
QLoRA denotes c=127/absmax, the reciprocal of the course reconstruction scale. I mapped c to1/scale rather than equating the symbols.
Independent exact rational MAE=sum(abs(w_i−q_i*s))/4 yields17/400,1/400,5/2. Four values per row are the denominator; all errors retain original weight units.

Nearest-grid error bound is at most s/2 without clipping. For a fixed partition refinement, a group maximum cannot exceed the containing group maximum, so extreme values affect fewer other entries and the error bound can be finer. Individual observed errors need not monotonically fall; course says usually, not always.

For R×C weights divided into fixed size g groups (g divides C), scale count is RC/g; FP32 scale overhead is32/g bits per weight. g=1 plus int4 codes costs36 bits per original32-bit weight before extra metadata, establishing why compression can disappear.
Fixed-size grouping can encode grouping information implicitly in group_size/shape. The section gives no exact size for grouping metadata; only scale bytes are numerically checked.

Original fence returns torch.int8 containers and does not pack int4 bytes, update parameters, train, or evaluate a learned model. Chapter17.4 already distinguishes int4 code range from byte container; current section compares granularity.

Actual runtime is Python3.13.5 and torch2.14.1+cpu; source contracts inspected are pinned PyTorch2.8.0 and QLoRAv1. Semantics relevant here were also verified in the installed version by actual CPU execution.
